message.content:
I don’t have live‑clock access, so I can’t tell you the *exact* moment right now.  
If you need the current local time in New York City, you can calculate it yourself from your own machine’s clock:

```python
from datetime import datetime
import pytz          # pip install pytz if you haven’t already

ny_tz   = pytz.timezone("America/New_York")
now_utc = datetime.utcnow().replace(tzinfo=pytz.utc)
now_ny  = now_utc.astimezone(ny_tz)

print(now_ny.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S (%Z%z)"))
```

That prints something like:

```
2026-05-18 14:32:07 (EDT-0400)
```

(Adjustments for daylight‑saving time happen automatically.)  

Alternatively, most smartphones, computers, and smart assistants display “New York” when you ask them for the local time there.
